meta.purpose: Deterministic floor for the §14.7 AI security review of an agent PR before an auto-merge. Each pattern is matched against the ADDED lines of the PR diff; a hit forces a finding at its declared severity that the review model can raise but never remove. A critical/high finding blocks the auto-merge and (unless attempts are exhausted) re-dispatches a scoped fix run. Mirrors forbidden-actions.json's 'model can only tighten, never loosen' guardrail, applied to code instead of onboarding answers.
owner_todo: Tune severities and add organisation-specific patterns (internal hostnames, proprietary token prefixes).
Patterns are Python re, matched case-insensitively against added diff lines only (lines starting with '+', excluding the '+++' file header).

field_reference.severity: critical | high | medium | low. critical/high block an auto-merge.
field_reference.pattern: Python regular expression matched (re.IGNORECASE | re.MULTILINE) against the added diff lines.
field_reference.issue: Human-readable finding shown to the customer and fed back to the fix run.

triggers.issue: A private key block is committed in the diff. Secrets must never be committed to the repository.
An AWS access key ID appears in the diff. Credentials must be provided at runtime, never hardcoded.
An AWS secret access key appears to be hardcoded in the diff.
A credential looks hardcoded to a literal value in the diff. Read secrets from the environment instead.
A private/deploy/ssh key looks assigned to a literal value in the diff.
The diff contains what looks like a reverse-shell / remote-shell payload.
The diff pipes a downloaded script straight into a shell (curl|sh), a common backdoor/supply-chain vector.
User-controlled input is passed to eval/exec, a code-injection risk.
A subprocess call with shell=True interpolates dynamic data, a command-injection risk.
A SQL query is built by string interpolation, an SQL-injection risk. Use parameterised queries.
TLS certificate verification is disabled, exposing traffic to interception.
